3.measure_note: legacy_colAB UNDERLINE form (four per-column underlines per line, text sitting ABOVE its rule), skew -0.3 deg. The FULL-WIDTH rowbands.py scan returned only 16 rules and MISSED the faint rule at ~78.9, leaving a DOUBLE band [75.25,82.73] spanning two printed lines (the §F6 hazard) — the `--col 80.4,89.9` amount-column recovery returned the clean 17-rule ladder 22.88/26.61/30.33/34.11/37.84/41.59/45.31/49.02/52.74/56.47/60.20/63.93/67.65/71.38/75.11/78.83/82.56 at pitch 3.73 (the amount column's rules sit ~0.17 pct ABOVE the full-width values because of the negative skew). Row 1 has no rule above it and its band is extrapolated one pitch up to 19.15. So the grid has SEVENTEEN usable lines (§H1) and the filer used all seventeen. THREE-CROP PROOF at 900 dpi --value on the bands stored here: pct:80.4,19.15,10.0,3.73@p3 rendered the printed 'Amount' header over '$50.00' (the recorded row-1 amount — the §A1 control therefore shows the filer did NOT skip line 1); pct:80.4,78.83,10.0,3.73@p3 rendered '$23.57' (the recorded row-17 amount); and the §B5 one-past-the-end control pct:80.4,82.56,10.0,3.73@p3 rendered '5690.79' — which is NOT an eighteenth entry but the printed 'Subtotal for this page' figure, and it EQUALS the sum of the 16 cash rows above it, i.e. the §H4 in-grid-subtotal signature rather than the §F1 below-the-rule row. A further control at the split of the missed rule, pct:80.4,75.11..78.83, rendered '$50 (In Kind)' distinct from row 17, confirming the doubled band really held two lines. The stored amount band [80.40,90.40] extends ~0.7 pct past the printed underline segment (which ends at 89.70) to the printed border, per §G2; no figure on this page reaches even the underline's end, so nothing clips.

4.measure_note: Same underline grid as p3, skew -0.4 deg, pitch 3.72. The full-width scan again returned a DOUBLE band at BOTH ends (missing rules at ~28.4 and ~80.6); the `--col 80.2,89.5` amount-column scan recovered 24.47/28.22/31.95/[35.68 interpolated, the one rule neither scan caught]/39.43/43.15/46.86/50.56/54.31/58.06/61.74/65.47/69.20/72.97/76.70/80.43/[84.15 interpolated, detected at 84.32 by the full-width scan] = 17 rules; row 1 extrapolated one pitch up to 20.75. Seventeen lines, all seventeen used. FOUR-CROP PROOF at 900 dpi --value on the bands stored here: pct:80.2,20.75,10.5,3.72@p4 rendered the 'Amount' header over '$112.09' (row 1 as recorded; the filer did not skip line 1); the two crops either side of the first missed rule rendered '$17.12' (row 2) and '$42.00' (row 3) separately, proving the doubled band held two lines; pct:80.2,80.43,10.5,3.72@p4 rendered '$2789.90' (row 17 as recorded); and the §B5 one-past control pct:80.2,84.15,10.5,3.72@p4 rendered '4572.10' — the printed 'Subtotal for this page', equal to the sum of the 17 rows above it (§H4), not an eighteenth entry. Amount band widened to the printed border per §G2; the largest figure ($2789.90) renders complete with white space to its right, so nothing clips on this page.

5.measure_note: Same underline grid, skew -0.6 deg, pitch 3.73; the `--col 80.6,90.1` amount-column scan gave 24.47/31.92/39.42/43.15/46.85/50.58/54.33/58.06/65.46/69.19/72.94/76.69/80.44 and the full-width scan gave the complements, together fixing a 17-rule ladder (missing members at 28.20, 35.65, 61.79 and 84.17 interpolated on the fitted pitch). Row 1 extrapolated one pitch up to 20.74. The filer used only lines 1-4; lines 5-17 are printed and empty. PROOF at 900 dpi --value on the bands stored here (every written row proved, since there are only four): row1 pct:80.6,20.74,10.5,3.73@p5 rendered the 'Amount' header over '$228.66'; row2 rendered '$49.50'; row3 rendered '647.22' (printed with NO dollar sign, unlike every other cell on the filing); row4 pct:80.6,31.92,10.5,3.73@p5 rendered '$50.54'. The §B5 one-past-the-end control pct:80.6,35.65,10.5,3.77@p5 rendered an EMPTY cell between two printed rules — so there is no §F1 row continuing below the last written line, and the band list is not off by one. Amount band widened to the printed border per §G2; no figure on this page approaches the edge.
